briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Toasts Award Season and Court Wins While National Rescheduling Clock Ticks
briefs.top: Michigan operators have real reasons to celebrate this week — fresh Zalympix hardware, new Ann Arbor-area storefronts, and an expedited court review of the hated 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, psychedelics keep racing toward FDA approval and investor sentiment on cannabis rescheduling is climbing even as a DEA judge hits pause on the hearing record.

local.text: Zalympix 2026 crowns Michigan's top flower, rosin — Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom took best overall flower and Hytek's Oishii Piña won best live rosin at the state's "Grammys of Cannabis," with YetiStash's Blue Limeade also medaling in both categories.
Bloom City Club opens new Ypsilanti store — the Ann Arbor-based retailer celebrated its newest Ypsilanti location with a month of cannabis-themed events in October.
Lume Cannabis opens new Ann Arbor storefront — the Michigan-based chain debuted its 2247 W. Liberty Street location with a Friday grand opening.

Governor hopefuls race to pledge tax relief — GOP candidate John James has pledged to repeal the 24% wholesale tax after industry executives backed his campaign, while Sheriff Chris Swanson's repeal push is also polling strong with voters.

Michigan Supreme Court fast-tracks wholesale tax appeal — justices ordered the Court of Appeals to expedite its review of the industry's constitutional challenge to the 24% levy, keeping the door open for relief.

national.text: Investors grow bullish on federal rescheduling odds — a new survey found respondents put 65% odds on rescheduling within six months and 47% said they're more bullish on multistate operators than six months ago.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin treatment nears FDA finish line — COMP360 holds an FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher after hitting its Phase 3 endpoints, with Compass targeting an NDA submission by Q4 2026.
DEA pauses rescheduling hearing, decision still looms — an administrative law judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding over a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13.
Rove cannabis brand expands into Canada — the U.S. vape brand announced its official entry into the Canadian market starting in Ontario, with more provinces planned.
Wall Street flags Trulieve as October buy — analysts cite the MSO's industry-leading 60% gross margins as a reason cannabis stocks could be turning a corner.
